newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo palladium ends mostly weaker, off early lows.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo palladium ends mostly weaker, off early lows.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo palladium futures ended mostly weaker on Monday but off early lows, as market sentiment remained bearish throughout the day, traders said.
Prices ranged from steady to 19 yen per gram lower, with benchmark April 1998 closing 19 yen down at 562 yen per gram.

The October, the December and the April contract plunged by the 22 yen per gram daily limit at the opening, on selling triggered by the expected resumption of Russia's exports of platinum group metals (PGM) to Japan.
The market recovered from the early tumble as individual investors, who hold massive short positions on TOCOM, later emerged to cover their shorts, traders said.
"Short-covering by local investors is likely to provide support in the near term," a brokerage house trader said.
Yen-based gold futures ended higher in all months. Prices ranged from two to eight yen higher, with benchmark April ending five yen higher at 1,272 yen per gram.
Traders said the weaker yen offset losses in New York on Friday. "Most players were reluctant to trade today, as the New York market is closed today," another trader said.
The New York precious metals market is closed on Monday for Memorial Day.
Spot gold was quoted at $342.50/343.00 per ounce at 0745 GMT, against $342.35/342.85 in New York on Friday.
Platinum futures ended steady to higher, on light buying from local investors, traders said. Benchmark April 1998 was up four yen at 1,359 yen per gram.
Silver futures were higher across the board.
Most-active April 1998 was up 3.3 yen at 178.8 yen per 10 grams.
